carla_support: Hey team — customer acme reports structured_output JSON contract changed after we promoted a model variant to stable (llama4b-v2). Their webhook parser now errors with a 400. Sample request they sent and both responses below.

acme_integration: Confirmed. Happened after your 11:04am promotion. Our parser throws `Unexpected token` when trying to parse the webhook payload.

carla_support: Minimal repro from customer: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"llama4b-v2","mode":"structured_output","stream":true,"input":"summarize: bullets"}'
```
Response (before promotion, expected):
```json
{"items":[{"id":"r1","text":"..."}],"response_meta":{"version":"structured_output_v1"}}
```
After promotion (what they receive):
```json
{"response_meta":{"version":"structured_output_v2"},"items":{"0":{"id":"r1","text":"..."}}}
```
The `items` array turned into an object and wrapper key name changed. Parser expects array -> fails.

deploy-bot: deployment: promoted model `llama4b-v2` from canary->stable at 2025-07-21T11:04:03Z (release id: r-20250721-42) :rocket:

olga_ml: @carla_support thanks — can you paste a request_id from customer logs? Also which SDK and parser are they using? streaming=true there is interesting.

carla_support: request ids: `req_84a9f2b1`, `req_84a9f2b2`. They're using internal webhook consumer in Node 18 with JSON.parse on the full payload (no stream-assembly). Customer says our webhook endpoint emits a final assembled JSON, but they sometimes get truncated or reshuffled keys.

sam_runtime: quick note — we changed the response assembler for streaming to yield chunked JSON objects sooner to reduce latency; also switched to a new serializer that preserves insertion order from model output. Might be related.

olga_ml: I pulled the two request traces. I can repro locally with streaming enabled and sequence length > 1024. The client-side parser sees interleaved chunk boundaries which our reassembler sometimes turns into object emissions instead of array emissions when model emits an index key. Hypothesis: model's tokenized output changed token boundaries for list markers leading the assembler to interpret the structure slightly differently.

olga_ml: Repro steps I'm using: 
1) POST with `stream:true`, `max_tokens:150`, `model:llama4b-v2`, input that prompts an array output (bullet list).
2) Subscribe to event stream and concatenate chunks.
3) Observe assembly: when a chunk boundary splits after `{"items":` we sometimes write `"items":{` instead of `"items":[` because model emitted an index token vs `[` token in the middle.

carla_support: Customer requests rollback or pin to previous variant. This is breaking production. SLA consequence.

mike_infra: We can route acme to `llama4b-v1` by creating a customer-specific routing rule (router rule id: rr-451). Will apply immediately as a mitigation. Also opening a rollback request for the global promotion if needed.

sam_runtime: Short-term mitigation: in the response assembler we can add a compatibility shim that normalizes `items` when it sees numeric keys into an array if we detect `response_meta.version` changes. I can patch a canary hotfix to the streamer assembly within the hour.

olga_ml: Plan: 1) Add streaming chunk reassembly fix to ensure structural tokens (`[`,`]`,`{`,`}`) are atomic tokens for the assembler. 2) Add regression tests for structured_output with streaming on multiple model tags. 3) Run canary build across our canary fleet and validate with the acme repro. ETA ~3h for canary, 8h for stable roll.

carla_support: Thanks — I've informed customer and applied the routing rule. They're requesting logs and an ETA; put the ETA in the ticket.

acme_integration: Appreciate the quick response. Pinning to the previous version is fine for now. Please notify when the fix lands so we can test before you promote again.

mike_infra: Rule rr-451 applied, acme now routed to `llama4b-v1`. Requesting internal postmortem channel once fix is out.

olga_ml: I'll attach the small repro harness in the ticket (curl + Node stream assembly snippet). If anyone from runtime wants to pair for the patch review ping me.

sam_runtime: I'll open a PR for the shim and include a test that replays the exact chunk boundaries from the traces.

carla_support: Marking this high-priority in the ticket and adding the customer contact to the incident. Thanks all. :pray:

acme_integration: Thank you — waiting on the test/patch so we can be unpinned.

(ends)
